rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

evidence_decisions.note: New paper evaluations use supported fresh evidence. CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes
Spread/total splits need exact source-line identity and remain display-only
Missing evidence retains the original forecast and is explicitly recorded
Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. All four overall samples need at least four games and fresh, matched CFBD evidence. Totals, underdog spreads, missing/stale samples and mixed evidence retain existing rules. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: Excerpts are truncated and no tests are certified (saved test evidence is for a different source snapshot), so these are review proposals, not confirmed defects. (1) nfl_props.py scenarios() lines 126-153: probabilities come from shifting prior-season position-level residuals onto today's mean (a homoscedastic additive error). This ignores heteroscedasticity (variance scales with the mean and line) and ties/clipping nuance; samples are not per-market calibrated. The code correctly labels it uncalibrated, and acceptance is held by ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED=False (line 30), which is appropriate. Candidate rows also drop pushes only via above/(above+below), so the bettor-facing p ignores push refund value in edge (line 300: edge=belief-1/decimal), a minor EV overstatement on whole-number lines. (2) nfl_props.py settle() lines 239-271: the stats cache silently skips when the season file is absent (continue at line 252), fine, but a missing snaps/roster file sets frames[key]=None without recording a source hash; cash is credited inside the same call as the ticket UPDATE, guarded by rowcount, which is safe against double settlement. Settlement basis 'snap_confirmed_zero' infers zero stats from snap presence; verify stats files always contain every player with offensive snaps, else a legitimately missing row is graded as 0 (definite risk, depends on data not shown). (3) props_book.py belief() line 173-180 and tick lines 382-383: belief is computed with seeded random bias and then overwritten by context.prop(...) probability, so edge is recomputed; verify the evidence layer does not stack bias a second time (possible double adjustment, hypothesis since evidence_decisions is not supplied). Also result_for uses points reconciliation only for NBA; NFL has no equivalent finality check beyond non-null scores.

Top observations (hypotheses/missing validation unless noted): (1) prop_research.py:147-150 refreshes the reference quote only from fresh_quotes and does not reject quotes observed at or after tip; with tip<=now rows moving straight to settlement, in-play or post-tip observations could be stored as the reference. It is labelled verified_closing_line=False, but verify props.fresh_quotes enforces pre-tip. (2) prop_research.py:126-131: the specialist forecast selects the contract by maximum edge across sides/books (max over options at line 129), then owner and consensus are scored on that same selected contract. The selection is conditioned on the minutes_usage model's own edge, so its Brier/log-loss/unit_return is optimistically biased relative to the benchmarks scored on its picks (selection effect, not leakage). Also line 136 marks owner_p/market_p as SHADOW_CANDIDATE at gap>=.02 with no calibration check, and the market consensus never uses the quote's own book prices, so gaps vs. the same price can be inconsistent. (3) bankroll_policy.py:48-62 uses base=min(initial,equity) but open_limit/risk accounting treats opposing tickets at full stake (intended, conservative). The per-sport reserve at line 52-54 applies only to the sportsbook regime for NBA/NFL game lines; the 'beyond_24h' room applies only when the new game is distant (line 50), while missing tip_utc on existing tickets counts as distant, which can silently starve long-dated allowance. Also prop_research.py:120 compares latest-appearance team_id to the snapshot team, and prop_research.py:118 assigns agents by player-id hash modulo a changing agent list, so identity can drift across runs (hypothesis). Tests are synthetic and do not certify model quality.

1) news_hypotheses.py:24-36/62-69 and context_trends.py:63-70: failure handling is fragile. In news_hypotheses.tick, if history_source or injuries load fails, `source`/`meta` are unbound, but the exception path only sets history=None, so later use is guarded only by that flag; however an exception type outside (OSError,ValueError,KeyError) (e.g., pandas ParserError/EmptyDataError, AttributeError on missing columns like fetched_utc/nba_team_id) will crash the whole tick before the transaction. Hypothesis, not definite bug. 2) Temporal/identity concerns: news_hypotheses.py:84/98 identity digest includes source sha256 and history sha256, so every new injury snapshot or history refresh creates a fresh hypothesis for the same game/player/stat, contradicting the comment at line 97 ('one predeclared hypothesis per player/stat/game') and enabling post-hoc cherry-picking and duplicate settled rows inflating Brier/unit stats in public() (lines 139-150). Likely definite design defect. (1) nfl_props.py scenarios() lines 126-153: probabilities come from shifting prior-season position-level residuals onto today's mean (a homoscedastic additive error). The code correctly labels it uncalibrated, and acceptance is held by ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED=False (line 30), which is appropriate. Candidate rows also drop pushes only via above/(above+below), so the bettor-facing p ignores push refund value in edge (line 300: edge=belief-1/decimal), a minor EV overstatement on whole-number lines. (2) nfl_props.py settle() lines 239-271: the stats cache silently skips when the season file is absent (continue at line 252), fine, but a missing snaps/roster file sets frames[key]=None without recording a source hash; cash is credited inside the same call as the ticket UPDATE, guarded by rowcount, which is safe against double settlement. Settlement basis 'snap_confirmed_zero' infers zero stats from snap presence; verify stats files always contain every player with offensive snaps, else a legitimately missing row is graded as 0 (definite risk, depends on data not shown). (3) props_book.py belief() line 173-180 and tick lines 382-383: belief is computed with seeded random bias and then overwritten by context.prop(...) probability, so edge is recomputed; verify the evidence layer does not stack bias a second time (possible double adjustment, hypothesis since evidence_decisions is not supplied). events.detail: Top observations (hypotheses/missing validation unless noted): (1) prop_research.py:147-150 refreshes the reference quote only from fresh_quotes and does not reject quotes observed at or after tip; with tip<=now rows moving straight to settlement, in-play or post-tip observations could be stored as the reference. (2) prop_research.py:126-131: the specialist forecast selects the contract by maximum edge across sides/books (max over options at line 129), then owner and consensus are scored on that same selected contract. The selection is conditioned on the minutes_usage model's own edge, so its Brier/log-loss/unit_return is optimistically biased relative to the benchmarks scored on its picks (selection effect, not leakage). Also line 136 marks owner_p/market_p as SHADOW_CANDIDATE at gap>=.02 with no calibration check, and the market consensus never uses the quote's own book prices, so gaps vs. the same price can be inconsistent. (3) bankroll_policy.py:48-62 uses base=min(initial,equity) but open_limit/risk accounting treats opposing tickets at full stake (intended, conservative). The per-sport reserve at line 52-54 applies only to the sportsbook regime for NBA/NFL game lines; the 'beyond_24h' room applies only when the new game is distant (line 50), while missing tip_utc on existing tickets counts as distant, which can silently starve long-dated allowance. Also prop_research.py:120 compares latest-appearance team_id to the snapshot team, and prop_research.py:118 assigns agents by player-id hash modulo a changing agent list, so identity can drift across runs (hypothesis). bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.

rules.basis: Distinct settled games; positive recent profit required for every heat label. Red also requires positive lifetime profit and ROI.
